# Card 3 on threat-v1 — strategist, 2026-11-20 (saved by Jarvis; the agent cannot write files)

Recommendation: Clever Concealment in, Boros Charm out. Keep Akroma's Will. Argument (★) unless marked evidence. No goldfish figures.

1. Rank. Concealment is the right card 3.
- Evidence: wipes ended games 001, 002 and 006; hand empty by turns 7-10.
- strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math ("assume the wrath", buy resilience instead of restraint); strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance (constant protection "useless against wraths"; a single-use instant "can cover the board"). Concealment is the second kind and convoke means no held mana.
- The doctor's shape count holds: Teferi's Protection is the only phase-out; the rest is indestructible/protection-from-colour, which the list's own Toxic Deluge and Meathook beat.
- Next: Lethal Scheme for Olivia Voldaren (removal 6 vs norm 8-10; Olivia is a Vampire and a repeatable ping engine, a real trade). Then Pact of the Serpent. Roaming Throne, Idol of Oblivion, Champion of Dusk lower.
- Sanctum Seeker is not in the branch; restoring it is a separate swap with its own cut.

2. Cut. Boros Charm is the weakest slot.
- Its indestructible mode is the shape Concealment replaces; its burn mode is 4 to one player; no draw.
- Akroma's Will is the better card: lifelink flying double-strike alpha pairs with Vito, Sanguine Bond, Enduring Tenacity, Blight-Priest. The Edgar gating is a cost, not a reason to cut the finisher.
- Selfless Spirit is a poor cut: a body that feeds sacrifice and drain triggers, works without Edgar; body count is the rebuild's fuel (strategy:sixty-card.threat-density).

3. How strong Edgar lists handle wipes.
- Evidence (recon): Teferi's Protection 30.9%, Boros Charm 29.3%, Akroma's Will 23.1%, Clever Concealment 11%; Walser: phasing counters sweepers and bounce.
- strategy:aristocrats.wipe-insurance: protection plus a rebuild package. The branch has the rebuild: Haruspex, Opportunist, Welcoming Vampire, Liliana. Furtado (strategy:deckbuilding.typal-density.lord-exposure): the Edgar deck "can get back online pretty quickly after one".
- Caveats: phasing returns at your untap, so the board is exposed again for a turn; a phased board cannot block or drain, so Concealment answers a wipe, it does not keep winning.
- Teferi's Protection stays (covers life, already a Game Changer).

4. Finisher loss.
- Keeping the Will: almost nothing changes. Bloodwitch is a drain-and-gain body, not an alpha; she does not replace the Will's lifelink swing.
- Cutting Boros Charm costs a little burn reach.

Open gaps: no strategy section on phasing vs wipe timing; no companion section on removal-count norms per commander (6 vs 8-10 has no citation).

## Rules quoted
- 702.26d: "Tokens continue to exist on the battlefield while phased out." Ruling 2023-02-04: "Permanents phase back in during their controller's untap step, immediately before that player untaps their permanents."
- 702.26g: "When a permanent phases out, any Auras, Equipment, or Fortifications attached to that permanent phase out at the same time… An Aura, Equipment, or Fortification that phased out indirectly won't phase in by itself, but instead phases in along with the permanent it's attached to."
- 702.26b: "a phased-out permanent is treated as though it does not exist. It can't affect or be affected by anything else in the game." Ruling 2023-02-04: "their triggered abilities can't trigger." Example under 702.26b: "You control a phased-out creature. You cast a spell that says 'Destroy all creatures.' The phased-out creature is not destroyed."
- 702.26a: "During each player's untap step, before the active player untaps permanents, all phased-in permanents with phasing that player controls 'phase out.' Simultaneously, all phased-out permanents that had phased out under that player's control 'phase in.'" 502.1: "This turn-based action doesn't use the stack."
- 702.51a (convoke): "…you may tap an untapped creature of that color you control rather than pay that mana… For each generic mana… you may tap an untapped creature you control…" 302.6 reaches only tap abilities and attacking, not convoke. Ruling 2024-01-12: "You can tap any untapped creature you control to convoke a spell, even one you haven't controlled continuously since the beginning of your most recent turn."
- Clever Concealment oracle: "Convoke… Any number of target nonland permanents you control phase out. (Treat them and anything attached to them as though they don't exist until your next turn.)"
